title: Hong Kong mulls AI facial recognition-enabled drones to police smoking ban at construction sites, 39 fines issued so far
content:
Authorities have issued 39 fines since a smoking ban at construction sites came into effect last month, with the Labour Department saying it is looking into equipping drones with facial recognition tools to better enforce the new law.

label: adverse
max_acceptable_basis: p90 of 3060 scored solutions articles in filtered_20260805_090909 (median 0.2437, p99 3.8698)
why_adverse:
Two independent failures, either one sufficient.

FIRST: it does not exist yet. The Labour Department estimates nine months to a year of research to integrate facial recognition into the drones, and no fine has been issued on drone evidence. Solutions is for initiatives that WORK. solution_concreteness (6.56) is the top dimension and it fired on a proposal: every concrete detail in the article — 1,400 sites inspected, 39 fines, 11 improvement notices, HK$3,000 and HK$400,000 penalties, a 60-80°C thermal threshold — belongs to the smoking ban already in force, not to the AI system being scored. The lens read an enacted policy's enforcement statistics as evidence for an unbuilt system described in the same article. This is a general trap worth generalising from: an article about a proposed extension to a working programme carries the working programme's evidence.

SECOND: the mechanism is the objection. The intervention is facial-recognition drones surveilling construction workers. Nothing in the rubric prices what an intervention costs the people it is applied to. equity_access (4.50) asks who benefits from a solution, not who is subjected to it, and there is no dimension between them. community_practice_strength (1.20) is correctly near-zero and correctly carries almost no weight.

Scope this row carefully. The underlying smoking ban is a defensible response to the Tai Po fire that killed 168 people, and a fix that learns "workplace safety enforcement is adverse" is worse than the bug. The adverse signal is specifically biometric surveillance as the enforcement mechanism, scored above p99 before it exists.
misleading_features: Enforcement statistics from the already-live ban (1,400 sites inspected, 39 fines, 11 improvement notices) read as evidence the AI-drone system works; it has issued zero fines and is 9-12 months from existing
Numeric specificity as a proxy for concreteness — HK$3,000 / HK$400,000 penalties and a 60-80°C thermal detection range make an unbuilt system read as engineered
A named government department with a stated delivery timeline reads as a governance intervention in force (governance_intervention_strength 5.25) rather than an announced intention
A high-casualty precipitating event (168 deaths in the Tai Po fire) supplies stakes that lift systemic_impact (5.19) without any part of the intervention being realised
No dimension prices the intervention's cost to its subjects: facial recognition applied to workers is invisible to the rubric, since equity_access scores who benefits and not who is surveilled
